charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For NagaCorp Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For NagaCorp Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For NagaCorp Ltd.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For NagaCorp Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For NagaCorp Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For NagaCorp Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For NagaCorp Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For NagaCorp Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For NagaCorp Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For NagaCorp Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
dcf.model_approach_note: 2026-10-23 one-pass fix after exit 3 (trip: 'Base case upside 168% with price in the upper half of the 10yr range (126%)'). (1) WACC +1.0pp regulatory single-point-of-failure premium, 11.5% -> 12.5% in all three scenarios (diagnosis candidate wacc_too_low; template low end). (2) growth_too_high NOT applied as a cap: the -9.9% FY2018-25 through-cycle CAGR is a pre-peak-to-post-COVID artefact; justification recorded in historical_growth. (3) No peak-earnings or exit-multiple fix: base already takes FY2026 revenue -7% off a 57% margin, and Gordon (10x at 12.5%/2.5%) binds below the 12x cap. Effect: base IV HK$5.95 -> 5.30, weighted HK$5.05 -> 4.51. NOTE on the trip itself: the price-position (126%) and historical-multiple figures in this block are an fx-direction artefact of scripts/sanity_check.py on a USD-reporting/HKD-quoted ticker (HKD price x fx_rate instead of / fx_rate: FY2018 printed price 75.47 = HK$9.63 x 7.8365; the current HKD price x 7.8365 compared against the raw, unconverted HKD 10-year series gives 1.2585). The real 10yr range position is 0% (the current price IS the 10-year low); real historical P/B 0.73-3.46x, EV/EBITDA 5.0-18.5x ex-FY2021, P/S 2.8-8.7x ex-FY2021. implied_multiples printed by the script are inflated by fx once (HKD IV against USD per-share metrics); divide by 7.8365 for the real figures below. The residual exit 3 after this fix is that artefact, not a valuation problem; one fix pass is the budget and no further driver changes were made.
